items.title: S&P 500 Positive Profit Surprises Trending Above 5-Year Average
items.summary: With earnings season progressing, some 86% of S&P 500 companies have reported a positive profit-per-share surprise for the quarter, which is above the five-year average of 78%, according to John Butters, a senior earnings analyst from FactSet.  S&P 500 companies are exceeding their earning per share estimates for the second quarter by 29.2% in aggregate, which is above the five-year average of 7%, FactSet found.  The blended earnings growth rate for the quarter, which includes actual earnings and estimates for the index constituents is 50.4%, the highest growth rate since the second quarter 2021's 91.6%.

items.title: July jobs report reveals unexpected loss of 23,000 jobs
items.summary: Friday's jobs report showed employers shed jobs last month, rather than adding 95,000 new hires that had been forecast by economists.

items.title: Trade Desk Stock Tumbles as Things Go From Bad to Worse. Here Come the Downgrades.
items.summary: Trade Desk  stock sank to the bottom of the  on Friday after the advertising technology company reported second-quarter revenue that fell short of expectations.  If the move holds, Trade Desk will close at its lowest level since January, 30, 2019, according to Dow Jones Market Data.  It’s been a tough stretch for Trade Desk shares, which have declined 63% this year and are down 74% over the past 12 months.

items.title: Atlassian Stock Surges 30% After Earnings. So Much for the Software Slump.
items.summary: Atlassian  shares soared around 30% in premarket trading Friday after the collaborative software maker reported better-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter results and issued optimistic guidance.  Atlassian reported quarterly earnings of $1.87 a share and revenue of $1.77 billion, up 28% from a year ago, late Thursday.
